agree.reason: The page is plain and believable, but nothing in it helps an owner who pays her cousin $600 a year at tax time see why $199 a month is worth it, so she has little reason to book.

honest.reason: Every claim matches the facts, and the $800 saving comes with an explicit no-promise; the one stretch is the headline's 'ran one', since Carla managed a salon rather than owned one.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw numbers are listed but never worked: the page doesn't give the yearly cost ($2,388), doesn't say that every client who kept their salon stayed, and doesn't frame the 9 savings reports as a share of 31 clients.

right_comparison.reason: The real alternative is a once-a-year tax-time bookkeeper at $600, and the page never describes it or what happens when books are only done once a year; it only mentions her old $149 price.

qualification.reason: The guarantee is specific and checkable: a missed 10th means that month is free, it started in January, and it is backed by an honest count of 3 misses; the limit of five new clients is also concrete, though 'this year' reads oddly in November.

objections.reason: Saying her own tax preparer keeps doing the return helps a little, but the page never says outright that her cousin can stay, and it doesn't take on the price gap; it spends space on the old price increase, which this reader wasn't asking about.

fit.reason: It runs to roughly 330 words of sales-page copy and ends with a button to book the call, as the brief asked.
